item.title: Healthcare Forum 2026 + Resource Fair — Fri Nov 13, 10:30 AM — The Backdrop @ Becoming Independent
item.description:
Healthcare Forum 2026 & Resource Fair
Tickets Are On Sale Now!
Last November, almost 300 people showed up for "What's Changing in Healthcare and What To Do Next," our Healthcare Forum & Resource Fair. The atmosphere was unbelievable.
Regional experts, healthcare providers, and community leaders came together to cut through the noise and connect Sonoma County families with real healthcare resources.
That same energy is coming back.
The same design team behind last year's forum is already curating this year's program. If last year was any sign, you'll want to be in the room.
More details on speakers and the program are coming soon.
For now, GET YOUR TICKETS!

item.title: Veterans Tribute Luncheon November 13 — Fri Nov 13, 11:30 AM — Santa Rosa Veterans Memorial
item.description:
**Santa Rosa Rotary and Kiwanis Clubs to Host Veterans Tribute**
**Luncheon November 13**
**Retired Brigadier General Michael Warmack to deliver keynote address; veterans attend at no cost**
**SANTA ROSA, Calif. —** Six local Rotary and Kiwanis clubs will jointly host the Santa Rosa Veterans Tribute 2026, a luncheon honoring America’s veterans, on Friday, November 13, from 11:30 a.m. to 1:30 p.m. at the Santa Rosa Veterans Memorial Building, 1351 Maple Avenue, Santa Rosa.
The hosting collaboration includes the Rotary Club of Santa Rosa, Rotary Club of Santa Rosa East/West, Rotary Club of Santa Rosa Sunrise, Rotary Club of Valley of the Moon, Kiwanis Club of Santa Rosa and Kiwanis Club of Oakmont.
The program will feature keynote speaker Brigadier General Michael Warmack, U.S. Army (retired), and performances by the CCLA Marching Band and the Elsie Allen High School Marching Band & Drumline
Tickets are $20 each, with no cost to veterans. Rotary and Kiwanis members are encouraged t

item.title: Paint & Sip with Genevieve Elkin — Fri Nov 13, 5:30 PM — Petaluma Arts Center
item.description:
Join us for a relaxed and social paint & sip evening. You'll be guided step-by-step through painting a scenic view using acrylics, with plenty of room to make it your own.
Whether you follow along or add your own creative twist, the focus is on enjoying the process and having fun. Sip on a beverage, come with friends or meet new ones, and settle into a laid-back night of painting and connection. No experience needed - just show up and create.
Genevieve Elkin was Born and raised in Mill Valley, California and is a multidisciplinary artist now based in Petaluma. She earned a BFA in Illustration from Parsons School of Design and has professionally managed art departments, supporting artists and new media on high-profile projects. Genevieve loves painting, drawing, and exploring ceramics, and enjoys helping students experiment, have fun, and develop their own creative voice.
To learn more:@gennaelkin
Sponsored by
Source: North Bay Bohemian

item.title: Bay Area Cinema #8 — Fri Nov 13, 6:30 PM — The Exchange
item.description:
Bay Area Cinema, a free pop-up microcinema showcasing short films, is a family friendly event. Our 8th show will feature films from a variety of genres (animation, documentary, music videos, narrative, and experimental) which explore themes and subjects such as environmental, human interest, and BIPOC/ethnic.
We had a little over 200 short films from around the country and locally submitted for Bay Area Cinema #8. We are proud to announce that we have selected 13 filmmakers and we would like to share their amazing films at our next screening, (during the Vallejo Art Walk) at The Exchange, 617 Marin Street, on Friday, November 13th, 2026, doors open at 6:30pm, showtime is 7pm-9:30pm. Like always, filmmakers will be there for a Q&A with the audience immediately following the screening. Mark your calendars, this will be a great show! This is a free event with $10 suggested donation.
Source: North Bay Bohemian

item.title: Write & Collage: Words, Images & Memory — Sat Nov 14, 10:00 AM — Petaluma Arts Center
item.description:
Join Marlene Cullen for a creative two-hour experience that brings writing and collage together. In the first hour, guided freewriting prompts invite you to explore memorable moments, stories, and experiences in a welcoming, supportive environment. In the second hour, transform those reflections into a visual expression using images, colors, and textures.
No writing or art experience is necessary—just bring your curiosity and a willingness to explore.
Bring: A notebook and pen. Collage materials will be provided, and you're welcome to bring a favorite poem, magazines, photographs, or other materials you'd like to incorporate.
Marlene Cullen is the founder of Writers Forum and creator of Jumpstart Writing Workshops. Through her website and blog, The Write Spot, she shares resources and inspiration to help writers discover and develop their voices.
The Write Spot anthologies edited by Marlene are collections of short stories, poems, and vignettes with prompts to encourage writing.
S

item.title: Jerry Seinfeld — Sat Nov 14, 8:00 PM — Luther Burbank Center for the Arts
item.description:
Jerry Seinfeld has been hailed for his uncanny ability to joke about the little things in life that relate to audiences everywhere. His latest Emmy®-nominated Netflix projects include Jerry Before Seinfeld and 23 Hours to Kill, along with the highly acclaimed web series, Comedians in Cars Getting Coffee. Seinfeld has also starred in, written, and produced movies \(Comedian, Bee Movie\), directed and produced a Broadway hit \(Colin Quinn: Long Story Short\), and wrote three best-selling books \(Is This Anything?, The Comedians in Cars Getting Coffee Book, and Seinlanguage\) and a children’s book \(Halloween\). He stars in the Emmy-nominated comedy film, Unfrosted, which he directed, co-wrote, and produced. Seinfeld continues to perform both nationally and internationally.
Source: North Bay Bohemian, Visit Santa Rosa

item.title: Healdsburg Garden Club General Membership Meeting — Mon Nov 16, 1:00 PM — Villa Chanticleer Annex
item.description:
The next General Membership meeting will take place on Monday, November 16, 2026, at the Villa Chanticleer Annex (860 Chanticleer Way, Healdsburg). The meeting begins at 1:00 PM, followed by a light potluck luncheon and an educational program. Guests are welcome.
Our speaker for November is Bruce Horace Robinson, a Sonoma County Master Gardener, Class of 2016. He will give a presentation on "Good Bugs, Bad Bugs." Bruce has been a gardener since childhood. After many years of changing garden strategies, he has become a strong believer in creating a garden that is in balance and harmony with nature by using biological controls and adhering to sustainable gardening principles.
The public is invited to attend this presentation starting at 2:00 PM at the Villa Chanticleer Annex.
Source: North Bay Bohemian

item.title: Standing Tall: The Story of the Mare Island 21ers — Fri Nov 20, 6:00 PM — Vallejo Naval and Historical Museum - Heritage Chamber
item.description:
A living history panel on the story of the Mare Island 21ers, the Black shipyard workers who took on the U.S. Navy.
On November 17, 1961, twenty-one Black workers at the Mare Island Naval Shipyard did something few people dared: They filed a formal complaint of racial discrimination against the United States government.
They were pipefitters, mechanics, welders, painters, and laborers who had endured years of unequal treatment in hiring, training, promotions, and pay. They filed their complaint before the Civil Rights Act of 1964 and before the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission existed. They put their jobs on the line anyway. Represented by attorney Charles Wilson, they pressed their case against the federal government at a time when few would, and their stand helped build the pressure that changed federal employment law.
Sixty-five years later, the Vallejo Naval & Historical Museum marks the anniversary with an evening of living history, right here in the city where it happen

item.title: Crossing Delancey - a Curtain Call Theatre Production — Fri Nov 20, 7:30 PM — Curtain Call Theatre Russian River Hall
item.description:
She knows exactly the kind of guy she wants, but grandmother Bubbe and the matchmaker think differently.
This nostalgic favorite was made into a beloved film in 1988. It is a love story about Izzy, a thoroughly modern woman with not the greatest taste in men. Her grandmother Bubbe is desperate to get her married. Enter Henka, the matchmaker with a New York accent so sharp it could cut cheese, and Sam Posner, the pickle man with the heart of a poet. Will Izzy make the right choice? Doors open half an hour early for a photographic slideshow about New York’s Lower East Side, and some special snacks: Babka and Brooklyn Egg Creams. Don’t miss this delightful romantic comedy suitable for ages 8 and up.
Playwright: Susan Sandler
Director: Amanda Claiborne
Starring: Kathy Ping-Rogers, Kimy Martinez-Knight, Nick Stewart, Karen Clancy and Jake Hamlin

item.description:
The Sonoma County Genealogical Society Presents
The Mayflower: An Interesting Mix of Passengers
Presented by Suzanne Brayer
In 1620, an English merchant ship, The Mayflower, left Southampton England for the New World carrying 102 men, women, children and a crew of 30. What motivated them to embark on this incredibly dangerous journey into the unknown? In addition to the passengers; the ship, the journey, The Mayflower Compact, the early history of the Plymouth Colony and the ubiquitous myths, these all make for fascinating stories.
Ms. Brayer has a BA from Indiana University and a MA in history and education from Arizona State University. She enjoyed a career in secondary education for 30 years. After retirement, she became a professional genealogist. item.title: Introduction to Drawing Portraits From Photos (3 Session Class) — Wed Nov 25, 6:00 PM — Sebastopol Center for the Arts
item.description: Introduction to Drawing Portraits from Photos November 4th, 11th, and 18th 6:00-9:00pm $150.00 + $15.00 Materials Fee = $165.00 Age Restricted to 18+ About this class: In this three week course, students will learn and practice observational skills and fundamental drawing techniques while learning the basics of drawing portraits from photographs. Drawing human faces requires the same basic drawing skills that one employs for any subject – observing proportion, flattening shapes, and utilizing line or value to convey volume. But the conceptual weight of human faces tends to intimidate artists. When drawing any subject, the hardest skill is simply learning to see, a skill that anyone can be taught, practice, and hone. This course will focus on the practice of looking, and discovering strategies to find objectivity when rendering portraits.
